title: Implement and Integrate a Configurable URL Stripping Preprocessing Step
description: The ChatRipple-C pipeline analyzes sentiment in text messages. Currently, URLs (e.g., 'http://example.com') are treated as regular words, which can skew the sentiment analysis results. This task involves adding a new preprocessing step to strip these URLs from the input text. To ensure flexibility, this new feature must be configurable, allowing it to be enabled or disabled at compile time.

project_spec.name: ChatRipple-C: Event-Driven Social Sentiment Pipeline
project_spec.description:
ChatRipple-C is an easy-level C project that demonstrates how real-time social conversations can be mined, modeled, and visualized through an event-driven NLP pipeline. The application listens to public chat rooms (e.g., IRC, Matrix or Discord gateways) and raises an event every time a new message arrives. Each event triggers a lightweight preprocessing stage (tokenization, stop-word removal, emoji normalization) followed by a bag-of-words sentiment classifier exported to ONNX. Events then fan out to downstream subscribers: (1) a live dashboard that graphs aggregated sentiment waves, (2) an experiment-tracking module that logs feature statistics, predictions, and model version meta-data, and (3) an automated-retraining worker that queues nightly jobs when data-drift thresholds are exceeded.

The project highlights social interactions by focusing on community mood shifts and conversation spikes. Built on a Pipeline Pattern, every processing step pushes an event onto a ZeroMQ bus so new modules (e.g., toxicity detection or language identification) can be hot-plugged without touching the core. Observer Pattern subscribers—visualizer, evaluator, retrainer, and version registry—receive notifications independently, enabling clean separation of concerns. MLOps principles are showcased through model_versioning (each retrain stores metrics and weights in a local directory structure with semantic version tags) and experiment_tracking in an embedded SQLite database that can later be uploaded to a full MLFlow stack.

Overall, ChatRipple-C gives beginners a tangible, social-centric example of how event streams, simple NLP models, and MLOps practices converge in C.
dependencies: ONNX Runtime C API (load/run the sentiment model)
